HM02-q01-mgo9su: The key marking is the HazMat's name, matching the shipping paper; the carrier's name is not it.
The most important marking is the material's name, the same as on the shipping paper.
HM02-q02-rc0p1c: Labels go close together, near the proper shipping name, not on opposite sides.
Put multiple labels close together, next to the proper shipping name.
HM02-q03-tckfz5: Labels match the hazard class; packages with liquid containers get orientation arrows pointing up.
Placards go on vehicles and bulk packages; packages with liquid containers get upright arrows.
HM02-q04-x2wzkk: Don't just haul an unfamiliar material; compare paper with markings and ask the shipper to contact your office.
The handbook's step for an unfamiliar material is to ask the shipper to contact your office.
HM02-q05-t85kuf: A pest control or agricultural supplier is a listed clue that a load may be HazMat.
Cylinders and drums are a listed clue that a load may be HazMat.
HM02-q06-jiol83: You must carry the manifest yourself, sign it by hand, and treat it as a shipping paper.
The manifest has no weight cutoff; 1,001 lb is the Table 2 placard rule.
HM02-q07-vbiput: Not just any carrier; only another registered carrier or a disposal/treatment facility.
Hand hazardous waste only to another registered carrier or a disposal/treatment facility.
HM02-q08-66o947: Placard before you drive; an improperly placarded vehicle moves only in an emergency.
Even a short move needs proper placards; only an emergency to protect life or property allows it.
HM02-q09-97m2ox: 9.84 inches is the placard size; placards must be at least 3 inches from other markings.
There is a set distance: at least 3 inches from any other markings.
HM02-q10-cc9696: Level words and numbers reading left to right is a placard rule.
A background of contrasting color is a placard rule.
HM02-q11-v8483w: The front placard may be on the front of the tractor or the trailer, not only the trailer.
The front placard may be on the front of the tractor or the trailer; the bumper is not specified.
HM02-q12-ii901o: 3 inches is the spacing from other markings; placards are at least 9.84 in (250 mm) square.
Placards are larger than package labels: at least 9.84 inches (250 mm) square, on point.
HM02-q13-bq3o56: 1,001 lb is the Table 2 threshold; Table 1 materials need placards in any amount.
Table 1 applies to any amount in any packaging, not only bulk.
HM02-q14-2xr8cu: 2.2 non-flammable gases are Table 2, placarded at 1,001 lb or more.
Class 8 corrosives are Table 2, placarded at 1,001 lb or more.
HM02-q15-meaoz4: 1.1 mass explosives are Table 1, placarded in any amount.
2.3 poisonous/toxic gases are Table 1, placarded in any amount.
HM02-q16-b4kws1: Add all Table 2 amounts: 600 + 500 = 1,100 lb, which is 1,001 or more, so placards are needed.
Waste or not, the Table 2 total of 1,100 lb requires placards.
HM02-q17-0vq4ud: The 1,001-lb total includes the weight of the package.
Add the Table 2 amounts from all shipping papers on board, not just one shipment.
HM02-q18-p2h3ph: DANGEROUS placards are optional, never required; you may always placard each class separately.
DANGEROUS placards apply only to Table 2 classes, not Table 1.
HM02-q19-e93zpf: With 2,205 lb or more of one class loaded at one place, DANGEROUS is not allowed; use its specific placard.
That amount is over 1,001 lb, so it needs placards: its own specific placard.
HM02-q20-qbxtu5: The 1,000-pound exception does not apply to INHALATION HAZARD; placards are needed in any amount.
INHALATION HAZARD needs POISON GAS or POISON INHALATION placards, not a DANGEROUS placard.
HM02-q21-9s0mk3: The 1,000-pound exception does not apply; the DANGEROUS WHEN WET placard is needed in any amount.
A dangerous-when-wet secondary hazard needs the DANGEROUS WHEN WET placard in addition to class placards.
HM02-q22-xwtswj: The class or division number goes in the lower corner, not the top.
The class or division number goes in the lower corner of the placard, not the center.
HM02-q23-woj2jv: 5.1 oxidizers have the OXIDIZER placard in Table 2.
2.1 flammable gases have the FLAMMABLE GAS placard in Table 2.
HM02-q24-4juz2r: Class 9 is a Table 2 class, and its placard is not required for domestic transportation.
The Class 9 placard is not required for domestic transportation.
HM02-q25-cc1p5v: A bulk package holding only residue must still be placarded.
The 1,001-lb rule doesn't apply to bulk packaging; even with only residue it is placarded.
HM02-q26-sdywtg: 119 gallons or less is nonbulk packaging; bulk means more than 119 gallons.
Bulk packaging is defined as a single container with a capacity greater than 119 gallons.
